The problem

Fashion bets six months of cash on a guess.

A maison learns whether a bag sells only after it has made it. Three rounds of physical samples, a photo shoot, a first production order. If it flops, it ends up on sale. If it sells out, there is no stock left to sell.

How it works · one product, end to end

The Cognac Cabas, from sketch to GO.

A structured leather tote for a Milanese maison. Every image below was generated on the platform from one sketch.

01 · Brand

The brand book sets the boundaries.

The house uploads its corporate identity document: brand book, guidelines, manifesto, even as a PDF or a scan. Evolus AI reads and summarises it, and Sartoria turns it into the brand's characteristics.

Every product after that is written inside them: the house's materials and colours, and never what the brand rules out.

Read by Evolus AI from the Aurenzi Milano brand book.

02 · DNA

The sketch becomes a product of the brand.

The designer uploads a sketch and two lines of brief. Sartoria reads the constraints and locks them into the product's DNA, its identity card that every later image must respect.

Images are drawn by Qwen Image 2.1 with a brand LoRA trained on the maison's leathers, stitching and finishes. Open weights, so it runs on our own GPUs and the brand's unreleased designs stay private.

03 · 3D

A 3D prototype checks the proportions.

From the product photo we rebuild a 3D model with TRELLIS.2, Hunyuan3D 2.1 and SAM 3D, and the team keeps the best one. The mesh fixes the true size, so the bag keeps its 28 × 22 × 10 cm proportions in every photo and video that follows.

TRELLIS.2Hunyuan3D 2.1SAM 3D
04 · Content

Everything a launch needs, ready for social.

Product shots, a lifestyle scene, on-model photos, editorials, reels with virtual creators and the product page. The same bag in every frame.

All the content for the Cabas took about 40 minutes of compute and $5.

05 · Test

Real audiences, before production.

Approved content becomes a social campaign on Instagram, TikTok and Pinterest in four countries, pointing to a pre-order page.

Each asset is measured. The lifestyle scene brings a pre-order for €37, less than half the product photo.

Pre-orders40

In the demo, audience response is simulated from the brand's past launches.

06 · Decide

Statistics make the call, not generative AI.

The forecast compares this test with the brand's past launches using classical statistics, so the order quantity can be explained line by line.

GO
Forecast sell-through74.5%
Target 65%Units to order: 710
07 · Iterate

Customers rewrite the product.

Gemma 4, Google's open model, running on AMD GPUs through AMD Token Factory, reads the test results and the comments in four languages and turns them into changes to the design, the content and the order.

One click writes the change into the DNA, and the next round starts corrected.

At the end, Evolus AI condenses the verdict, forecast, comments, actions and risks into three bullets management can read in a minute.

Summary for management · Evolus AI
  • 10-day test of the Cognac Cabas: €2,500 budget, 234,000 people reached, 40 pre-orders.
  • The lifestyle scene brought a pre-order at €37, against €91 for the product photo. Forecast sell-through 74.5% against a 65% target.
  • GO: order 710 units. 15% of comments ask for a crossbody strap, others a zip pocket.

Built on open models

Open weights, trained on the brand.

Trainable

A LoRA teaches Qwen Image the maison's style. Closed image models can't be fine-tuned like that.

Private

Image models run on our own GPUs, so sketches and unreleased collections never reach a third party.

Swappable

When a better 3D model ships, we plug it in without touching the rest of the pipeline.
